# relaybay

> relaybay is a local, open-source live board and MCP server for people who run many Claude Code sessions across many repositories. Sessions create and update tasks through MCP tools (Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp, Bearer token) and Claude Code hooks report session status; the owner watches projects, tasks, stages and reports update in the browser. Python 3.12+, FastAPI, SQLite, MIT license, no telemetry.

Stages are plan, dev, review, test, live, done. Every session should read `project_snapshot` first, pass its session on writes, keep `next_step`, `waiting_on` and `progress` current, and end every stage with `report_add` whose first line is `state · size · gist`.

## Docs

- [Specification](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/SPEC/): how relaybay behaves now: concepts, board, MCP contract, hooks, setup, working rules, security model, configuration, data model
- [Install with your coding agent](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/getting-started/agent-install/): an idempotent install-and-connect procedure for an agent, dry run first, apply only after the user agrees
- [MCP tools guide](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/mcp-tools/): how the tools and resources work together, with results and examples
- [MCP reference](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/reference/mcp/): every tool and resource with its parameters, generated from the live registry
- [Connect Claude Code](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/connect-claude-code/): MCP registration, the instruction snippet for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, hooks with `relaybay setup`
- [Install and run](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/getting-started/install/): `uv tool install relaybay`, `uvx`, `pipx` or Docker on Windows, macOS and Linux; first run and the token
- [CLI reference](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/reference/cli/): `serve`, `token`, `setup`, `doctor`, `demo`, `hook`
- [Configuration reference](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/reference/configuration/): `config.toml` keys, environment variables, flags
- [Policy reference](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/reference/policy/): the policy layers, keys, built-in guard rules and secret detectors, presets; JSON Schema

## Optional

- [Architecture](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/architecture/): processes, modules, data model, transports, security layers
- [Roadmap](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/ROADMAP/): versions and status
- [Design documents](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/design/): upcoming steps
- [Troubleshooting](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/how-to/troubleshooting/): `relaybay doctor --json` and what each failing item means
- [Import and export markdown](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/how-to/markdown-import-export/): `relaybay import` and `export`, layout, dry run, conflicts
- [Intake from chats and e-mail](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/how-to/intake/): watchers, matching to the waiting task, the autonomy switch, the backlog
- [Move to the desktop program](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/how-to/desktop-from-source-server/): from a server run in a source checkout to the installed program, same data folder, hooks via `relaybay-hook`, roll back
- [Docker server, desktop client](https://codenator81.github.io/relaybay/how-to/docker-server-with-desktop-client/): compose file, token from the volume, external mode, TLS or SSH tunnel, `allowed_hosts`
- [Source code](https://github.com/Codenator81/relaybay)
